about: What real machines, and the people using them, showed must change in Windstorm Pit Stop, and the version each change is due in. A lesson here is a gate, not a note: tests/test_promises.py refuses a version while a row due in it is not built, and refuses the version after it until the row says where it was proven on a real machine. Copied from Windstorm Tardigrade's PROMISES.json (the Windstorm skill standard, 2026-11-22).
how_to_use: A new lesson gets a row the day it is learned: what was seen, the promise, a codon in DNA-STRAND-MASTER-PLAN.md, the version it is due in, and a tracking issue.
When it is built: put the name of its test in 'test'. The test must exist and be the codon's Proof in the plan.
When it has been seen to work on a real machine: say which machine, which version and when in 'proven'.

'ship_in' moves only with a reason in 'moved_why'. A row whose owner is 'person' was seen by the person the plugin is for, on their own machine: its date moves only by their word, restated in 'moved_by_person'.
A row is never deleted. A promise that turns out wrong is closed by a row that says why.
A lesson that was heard and not taken goes under 'declined' with the reason, so that nothing is dropped without a word.

rows.seen: 2026-11-22, in an overnight stress test on a Linux laptop and an Intel Mac: a project-scope Pit Stop 0.6.1 in a test folder loaded the user-scope 0.1.4 instead; /hooks showed only 0.1.4's PreCompact hook, and nothing told the person. A session started with --plugin-dir pointing at 0.6.1 loaded 0.6.1 and no 0.1.4 hook: the start flag hides the older install; without the flag the older one wins. A restart is a second way to land on the older install: after a reboot the same session came back without its --plugin-dir flag and ran 0.1.4's hook again, with nothing said. Seen again by hand, 2026-11-25, a stock Linux virtual machine, Claude Code 2.1.332, no sign-in, one machine, once, from a served copy (steered: the newer copy a made 0.6.3, never published): with 0.6.2 at user scope and 0.6.3 for one project, 0.6.2's checkup run in that project and in a folder under it printed 'In <folder>, sessions load Pit Stop 0.6.2 (user), not 0.6.3 (project).' and 'To end it: claude plugin update windstorm-pit-stop@thewindstorm --scope user', and nothing from another folder; that command, typed as printed, moved the user-scope install to 0.6.3, and the checkup then said nothing. With an older copy from a second catalog at local scope, it printed 'To end it: cd <folder> && claude plugin uninstall windstorm-pit-stop@<catalog> --scope local'; typed as printed, it removed that install, and the checkup then said nothing. Which copy a session loads was not seen there (no sign-in).

That step is to be seen with 0.6.2, once the catalog pins a release. This covers the second half of the promise; the notice of G13.1 is still to build.

rows.seen: 2026-11-22, in that stress test, on a Linux laptop: a sudden reset cut a session in the middle of a 90-second Bash loop. The transcript ends on that tool_use with no result; on resume Claude Code shows 'No result recorded for 1 call' and 'Interrupted' and waits at an empty prompt. Pit Stop 0.6.1's PreCompact hook, run by hand on a copy of that transcript, answers hold (exit 2). Inferred and NOT seen: that Claude Code asks to compact such a session before a person types. On a macOS test machine on Claude Code 2.1.330, a session cut in the middle of a tool call by a clean reboot (not a sudden reset), leaving the same transcript shape, was resumed and waited three hours idle at an empty prompt, at 109K tokens with a 150K window and a 100K idle minimum, and was never asked. 2026-11-25, counts and field shapes only, from one machine's session files changed in the last four days: 90 files hold a hook_success entry whose hookEvent is SessionStart and whose hookName is 'SessionStart:resume', written by twelve Claude Code versions from 2.1.319 to 2.1.332 (2026-11-09 to 2026-11-25), so Claude Code starts SessionStart hooks on a resume and names the source; the hook's input field itself was not read.
rows.promise: A tool call with no result, made before the session's latest resume, counts as a break; a fresh start, /clear or a compaction never turns a running tool call into one. A guard for a case the transcript makes possible, not seen to occur on the Claude Code version tested.
rows.proven: Not seen on a real machine: on Claude Code 2.1.330 a resumed session cut in a tool call was not asked to compact in three hours idle (2026-11-22), so the hook was never called. What would count: a precompact.log line 'ALLOW break:cut-by-restart' from a real session, on any Claude Code version. This written reason does not hold 0.6.2 (accepted by the maintainers' reviewer, 2026-11-22).

A place it could not read (a unit or launch agent file, or a `crontab -l` refused, killed or silent) is named as not checked; no timer is made, fleet mode is NOT set up, setup answers 1, and the stop says what crontab answered (its exit code and first line, never the crontab's contents) and the one next step. `crontab -l` is read in the C locale; "no crontab for <user>" and no crontab program count as none there. A person whose own `crontab -l` shows no Pit Stop line runs setup with --crontab-has-no-pit-stop-line; a Pit Stop line that was read still wins. Rule 31 (B), read from each road that prints it (setup --help, with its docstring and the option's help, and the stop): no line naming the crontab carries a backtick, and each command the person is told to run (crontab -l; ls -l on a file not read, its name shell-quoted, held by a name with a space) stands alone on its own line; seen red on the strings of the 0.6.2 build first, one assertion at a time, and the space case red with the quote dropped. Rule 31 (vi): a name or words Pit Stop did not write holding a control character (unicodedata class Cc), U+2028/U+2029, or a byte that is not UTF-8 (class Cs) are shown changed (\x and the code) and the line says so, on nine roads, found by reading every place setup formats a path: step 6's could-not-read line, its crontab line and its schedules list; step 7's timer line; the earlier-install line; undo's launcher line and its two folder lines (step 5); the could-not-read line of the open-folder check (setup and status). For such a file no command is printed, only the step left (rename or remove it). A test plants a line feed, a carriage return, ESC and non-UTF-8 bytes and reads each road as printed, each seen red with its own cure taken out (the non-UTF-8 name ended setup with a traceback under a UTF-8 language before), and runs the changing function over the whole class. Seen on macOS 27 (arm64), in a clean test account: "crontab: no crontab for <user>", exit 1. On Ubuntu the "none" text is cron 3.0pl1's own, read from its program, not yet seen printed; cronie (the Fedora kind): not seen.
